## Research

I am a plant ecologist interested in how mountain plants respond to climate change at the European scale. My PhD at the University of Basel investigates large-scale redistributions of alpine vegetation during the Anthropocene — which species are moving, how fast, and what community-level consequences follow.

My work combines resurveys of historical vegetation plots across elevational gradients with continental-scale datasets, statistical modelling, and fieldwork in Norway and Svalbard. I am co-supervised by [Prof. Sabine Rumpf](https://rumpflab.github.io) (University of Basel) and [Prof. John-Arvid Grytnes](https://www.uib.no/en/persons/John-Arvid.Grytnes) (University of Bergen) within the [Zurich–Basel Plant Science Center](https://www.plantscience.ch).

Before Basel, I completed my MSc in Evolution and Ecology at the University of Tübingen, where I studied belowground water uptake strategies of grassland plants using stable isotopes, and later contributed to research on how plant functional traits shift under extreme drought.
